plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. This holds because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since my value is $42, I should bid exactly $42 to maximize expected profit, independent of the other bidders' rationality or beliefs about my strategy.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because the payment (second-highest bid) doesn't depend on my own bid unless I'm the winner, so overbidding risks paying more than my value for a win I shouldn't want, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $29, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay the appropriate second-highest price.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This holds because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $48, I should bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.
